name: WEC Energy Group
headline: A large Midwest electric and gas utility with a regulated return on a growing plan of approved projects.
what_short: Regulated Midwest electric and gas utility
what_it_does: WEC Energy Group delivers electricity and natural gas under regulated rates in four states, with Wisconsin as its largest. It also owns an interest in the American Transmission Company. A published plan calls for $33.4 billion of utility capital spending plus $4.1 billion for the transmission company from 2026 to 2030.
why_it_passed: Its earnings are a regulated return on approved capital, so the next ten years are easy to picture.
Its return on common equity runs 11% to 12%, though about 62% of its capital is debt.
The accounts can be followed line by line, and no dishonesty was found.
The analysis weighed management's ability in its favor.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what the utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $111.12 a share the price is above the whole value range ($67.70 to $78.29), and the buyer would be paid less than a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.31%).
watch: The capital added since 2020 ($11.4 billion) earned only about 5.1% before tax, below a Treasury bond.
Cash after capital spending was negative in every year from 2021 to 2025 (an average of minus $734 million), so the dividend and growth are paid from borrowing.
Illinois regulators have paused pipe spending, and the bonus for 2025 was paid at its 200% maximum; plan-share purchases were made above the analysis's value range.
